pain_points.cluster: Missing custom HTTP client support in langchain-anthropic blocks mTLS/cert-based authentication
Header/token forwarding failures for authenticated remote services (MCP server auth headers not propagated)
Inconsistent HTTP client handling across partner packages causing resource/config issues tied to client-level auth setup (Azure not reusing shared httpx client used for auth/connection config)
SSRF protection bypass via environment-variable based authentication/allowlist checks (unauthorized hosts bypassing validation)

authentication.suggested_prd_seed: Provide first-class, consistent support across LangChain partner packages for injecting custom authenticated transport (mTLS, custom CA bundles, proxy headers) into model clients, and close security gaps where authentication/authorization checks (header forwarding, SSRF allowlisting) can be bypassed or are inconsistently enforced.

pain_points.cluster: Approximate token counting (count_tokens_approximately) systematically over-counts non-text/multimodal content blocks
Providers return corrupted/inflated usage_metadata token counts that break downstream cost tracking
Lack of exact/native provider token counting APIs forces reliance on inaccurate approximations
No public, stable API for computing safe token-based message cutoffs for summarization/retention workflows
Token-count-based middleware triggers (context editing) behave incorrectly with persistent checkpointers, causing repeated re-counting/re-firing and wasted token-count calls

token counting and usage metadata.suggested_prd_seed: Improve the accuracy and reliability of LangChain's token accounting stack—fixing content-block-specific overcounting in count_tokens_approximately, guarding against corrupted provider usage_metadata, adding native provider token-count API support, and exposing a stable public API for token-based message cutoff/retention logic—so downstream cost tracking, context-window management, and summarization/eviction middleware behave correctly and efficiently even with persistent checkpointers.

pain_points.cluster: Provider-specific SSE/stream parsing incompatibilities causing zero chunks or dropped content
Streaming tool call argument fragmentation leading to premature execution with empty/invalid args
Duplicate/aggregated metadata fields from repeated terminal chunks during stream aggregation
Streaming + structured output interactions producing warnings or losing metadata (parsed field, response headers)
disable_streaming / streaming mode toggling logic bugs causing crashes or unintended full-stream disablement
Agent/graph-level abstractions not properly propagating token-level streaming, breaking callbacks like on_llm_new_token

streaming behavior and chunk handling.suggested_prd_seed: Improve robustness and correctness of LangChain's streaming pipeline across providers by fixing SSE/event parsing edge cases, ensuring tool-call argument chunks are only executed once fully assembled, deduplicating/aggregating terminal stream metadata correctly, preserving structured-output metadata (parsed objects, response headers) during streaming, and making disable_streaming and agent-level streaming controls behave predictably and propagate token-level events reliably."

pain_points.cluster: Silent data loss on document/text count mismatches in vector stores
Retriever result fusion / deduplication issues (EnsembleRetriever RRF score inflation from duplicate chunks)
Lack of multimodal metadata support in embedding interface limiting vector store integrations with multimodal providers
Missing concurrency/throughput optimizations in embedding providers used by vector stores (OpenAI, Mistral)
Limited configurability of vector store backend infrastructure settings (OpenSearch index creation settings)

retriever and vector store integrations.suggested_prd_seed: Improve the reliability and extensibility of LangChain's vector store and retriever integrations by enforcing strict validation on document/embedding count mismatches, deduplicating fused retrieval results, enabling multimodal metadata pass-through to embeddings, and exposing backend-specific configuration (e.g., OpenSearch index settings) and concurrency controls for embedding providers.

pain_points.cluster: HTMLSemanticPreservingSplitter extensibility limitations (no way to plug in a custom/tokenizer-based inner text splitter)
HTMLSemanticPreservingSplitter processes malformed/unsafe links (empty href, javascript: pseudo-links) creating invalid or unsafe markdown output
ExperimentalMarkdownSyntaxTextSplitter silently discards content when a code block is unclosed, causing silent data loss
ExperimentalMarkdownSyntaxTextSplitter has O(n²) performance due to list.pop(0) usage on large markdown documents
MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter lacks source line range metadata (start_line/end_line), hindering provenance/citation workflows for RAG

document loaders and text splitters.suggested_prd_seed: Improve the robustness, safety, and extensibility of LangChain's document splitters (HTMLSemanticPreservingSplitter and Markdown-based splitters) by fixing silent data loss and performance issues in markdown parsing, hardening HTML link handling against malformed/unsafe input, enabling pluggable tokenizer-aware sub-splitters, and adding optional source line-range metadata for provenance-aware chunking.

pain_points.cluster: Prompt template pretty-printing incorrectly renders partial variables

Output parsers (Pydantic/structured output) fail unpredictably when model output doesn't match expected schema shape (e.g., list vs string), producing confusing OutputParserException with no recovery guidance
Structured output serialization produces spurious PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue warnings
Poor error messages in prompt template loading/construction (bare ValueError with no context)

prompt templates and output parsers.suggested_prd_seed: Improve robustness and clarity of the prompt template and output parser stack by fixing partial-variable rendering in pretty_repr, providing clearer/documented recovery paths (e.g., with_fallbacks patterns) and error messages when structured/pydantic output parsing fails on shape mismatches, and eliminating spurious serialization warnings in structured output flows.

pain_points.cluster: Fragile/crashing parsing of malformed or fragmented tool call data
Lack of first-class API for programmatic/prefetched tool invocation without replaying full AIMessage+ToolMessage history (breaks with stricter model turn validation, e.g. Gemini 3.x)
Inadequate/undocumented tool error handling model - ToolException not catchable at agent/middleware level, handle_tool_error inconsistent across ToolNode vs @tool decorator
Tool call limiting/control middleware is reactive rather than proactive, leading to wasted tool calls and abrupt LLM behavior
Human-in-the-loop rejection handling ambiguity - concern that rejected tool calls could still be executed by ToolNode despite middleware intent

Incomplete observability/tracing metadata for tool call events (missing tool_call_id on on_tool_start, inconsistent with on_tool_error), hindering per-call attribution in streaming/parallel tool call UIs
Inconsistent support for structured output / function calling schemas across integrations (Pydantic schema unsupported in langchain-huggingface function calling)

tool calling and function calling.suggested_prd_seed: Improve the robustness and consistency of LangChain's tool/function-calling pipeline end-to-end—covering resilient parsing of malformed or fragmented tool call payloads, a first-class API for injecting precomputed/programmatic tool results without fragile message replay, unified and documented tool error handling (ToolException across @tool, ToolNode, and middleware), proactive tool-call-limit guidance, reliable human-in-the-loop rejection enforcement, complete tool_call_id tracing across all tool lifecycle events, and consistent structured-output/function-calling schema support across model integrations.

pain_points.cluster: Rigid, high-level agent abstractions lack composability and extensibility for advanced/custom workflows
Extra dependency surface and version-drift pain from add-on packages (deepagents) required for core-feeling capabilities like Agent Skills
Model-internal data (raw response metadata, provider-specific fields like image 'detail') is silently dropped by core abstractions, limiting monitoring, evaluation, and correctness
Partner/provider integrations lag behind upstream API changes (deprecated enums, deprecated tools), forcing developers to patch or work around outdated integration code
Assigning/triaging contributor PRs is unclear or slow, with multiple contributors independently duplicating fixes while waiting for maintainer assignment

developer experience.suggested_prd_seed: Improve LangChain's developer experience by exposing agent-building blocks (Deep Agent middleware, Skills, steering, workflow context injection) as first-party, composable primitives rather than locked-in high-level abstractions or external-package dependencies, while ensuring core message/response conversion paths preserve full metadata and partner integrations stay current with upstream provider APIs."

pain_points.cluster: Tool-call error handling is inconsistent and undocumented: ToolException doesn't propagate/catch as expected in middleware, handle_tool_error works for ToolNode but not @tool decorator, and agents don't reliably route errors back to the model for recovery.

Silent failures in structured output and agent loop control flow: agents can terminate or exit without surfacing errors (missing structured_response key, return_direct exiting on tool error) leaving developers with no signal that something went wrong.
Malformed/partial tool call payloads cause silent, all-or-nothing data loss instead of per-item error isolation, making debugging extremely difficult since no exception or warning is surfaced.
Bare exceptions with no descriptive message (e.g. raise ValueError with no context) across core and partner packages make it hard to diagnose the actual failure condition.

Integration-specific errors surface as confusing low-level exceptions (e.g. unexpected keyword argument TypeError) rather than clear, actionable error messages when using unsupported parameter combinations.

Model/provider-specific validation errors (e.g. Gemini rejecting replayed tool-call message structures) are cryptic and force fragile workarounds, with no first-class API to avoid constructing invalid message histories.

error handling and debuggability.suggested_prd_seed: Improve LangChain's error handling contract across agents, tools, and model integrations so that failures (tool errors, malformed API payloads, missing structured output, provider-specific validation errors) are surfaced with descriptive, actionable messages and consistently routed back to the agent/model loop for recovery instead of silently dropping data or terminating execution unexpectedly.

pain_points.cluster: Unnecessary device/host synchronization and redundant recomputation in embedding pipelines (HuggingFaceEmbeddings + Chroma) causing multi-fold slowdowns vs calling underlying libraries directly
Algorithmic complexity bugs (O(n^2) list.pop(0) usage) in text splitters causing severe slowdowns on large documents
Unconditional/eager heavy imports (e.g. transformers) at core module import time inflating cold-start/import latency across all users regardless of whether the feature is used
Cross-event-loop caching of async HTTP clients causing connection errors and reliability/latency issues under concurrent or multi-threaded async workloads
Lack of first-class support for safe parallel/concurrent middleware execution, forcing fully sequential middleware stacks and limiting throughput/latency optimization in production agent pipelines

performance and latency.suggested_prd_seed: Deliver a focused performance hardening pass across LangChain core and integrations that eliminates unnecessary synchronization/recomputation (embeddings), fixes algorithmic complexity bugs (text splitters), defers heavy/unused imports (core module load), resolves cross-event-loop resource sharing bugs (async HTTP clients), and enables safe concurrent execution paths (middleware) to reduce latency and improve reliability at scale.

pain_points.cluster: Upstream/dependency deprecations forcing breaking changes in integrations (IPEX/optimum-intel, OpenAI computer-use-preview, langchain-together version conflicts)
Silent behavioral regressions after refactors/reorganization (configurable metadata dropped, legacy serialization mapping pointing to stale module paths, bool->int coercion in merge_dicts)

Cross-package version coordination and compatibility breakage during dependency upgrades (Pydantic main breaking BaseLLM construction, staged/coordinated releases needed across langchain-core, langchain-tests, and partner packages)

backward compatibility and breaking chan.suggested_prd_seed: Establish a formal backward-compatibility policy and regression-test suite covering: (1) upstream/partner package deprecations (e.g., optimum-intel IPEX, OpenAI computer-use-preview, langchain-together version pins), (2) silent behavior changes introduced by internal refactors (metadata handling, serialization mappings, type coercion in streaming merges), and (3) coordinated, dependency-aware release sequencing across langchain-core and integration packages to prevent breakage from upstream library changes (e.g., Pydantic) or premature releases.

documentation gaps.suggested_prd_seed: The retrieved issues (#35836, #35514, #36211, #36214, #38226, #37452, #36067, #37018) are all functional bug reports or feature requests about runtime behavior (streaming, tool-call handling, provider API mismatches, vector store update logic, schema enforcement, and Hub manifest serialization) rather than reports of missing, unclear, or incorrect documentation, so no documentation-gap pain points can be substantiated from this issue set.

pain_points.cluster: Streaming/token-level output gaps across integrations (missing reasoning tokens, no token-level callbacks, broken SSE parsing)
Token usage/cost accounting inaccuracies (over-counting multimodal payloads, corrupted/inflated usage metadata, duplicated generation_info strings)
Provider/model inference and compatibility gaps (missing model prefix inference, provider-specific server errors from unconditional null params)

xylophone quarterly banana.suggested_prd_seed: Improve the reliability of LangChain's chat model integration layer by fixing token-level streaming/callback propagation (including reasoning tokens and SSE edge cases), correcting token usage/cost accounting bugs (multimodal token over-counting, duplicated generation metadata, corrupted usage figures), and closing gaps in provider/model auto-inference and payload construction that cause silent failures or server errors.
